# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 48

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 10

---

## Disagreement 1 — 48:1 agent attribution: "not I, but the Lord" vs. "not I who grants you this, but the Lord"

- **EMET:** "it is not I, but the Lord who grants you this"
- **LOGOS:** "it is not I who grants you this, but the Lord"
- **PNEUMA:** "This ability doesn't come from me — it comes from the Lord"
- **Greek:** *ouk emō...alla tou kyriou* — not of me but of the Lord
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "it is not I who grants you this, but the Lord" (LOGOS). The antithesis is important — the Shepherd disclaims credit. PNEUMA's paraphrase is accurate but loses the formal attribution.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 48:2 "overcome" vs. "prevail over"

- **EMET:** "you shall overcome all these things"
- **LOGOS:** "you shall prevail over all these things"
- **PNEUMA:** "you will conquer all these challenges"
- **Greek:** *panta tauta dynēsē* — you will be able (to do) all these things / overcome
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "you shall prevail over all these things" (LOGOS). "Prevail over" suggests a sustained victory; "overcome" is more momentary; PNEUMA adds "challenges" beyond the text.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 48:2 "double-minded" vs. "waver"

- **EMET:** "if you turn away from God and are double-minded"
- **LOGOS:** "if you turn away from God and waver"
- **PNEUMA:** "if you turn away from God and start wavering"
- **Greek:** *ean apostraphēs ap' autou kai dipsychēs* — if you turn away from him and are double-minded
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "if you turn away from God and waver" (LOGOS). "Waver" is a smooth English equivalent for *dipsycheō* (to be double-minded/hesitant).

---

## Disagreement 4 — 48:3 "not my own words" vs. "not my own message"

- **EMET:** "these things that I say are not my own words"
- **LOGOS:** "these things I say to you are not my own words"
- **PNEUMA:** "what I've been saying to you is not my own message"
- **Greek:** *tauta hā legō ouk aph' emautou eisin rhēmata* — these words I speak are not from myself
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "these things I say to you are not my own words" (LOGOS). "Words" (*rhēmata*) is precise; "message" (PNEUMA) generalizes.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 48:4 "charge you again" vs. "say it again as a charge"

- **EMET:** "I charge you again"
- **LOGOS:** "I charge you again"
- **PNEUMA:** "I'm saying it again as a charge"
- **Greek:** *palin soi parangellō* — I command/charge you again
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "I charge you again" (EMET/LOGOS). *Parangellō* = to give a charge/command; the military or official command nuance is present.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 48:4 "do not slack" vs. "do not slacken" vs. "don't let up"

- **EMET:** "do not slack"
- **LOGOS:** "do not slacken your effort"
- **PNEUMA:** "don't let up"
- **Greek:** *mē rhathumēsēs* — do not be slack/careless/idle
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "do not slacken" (LOGOS). "Slacken" captures the progressive loosening of effort that *rhathumeō* implies; "slack" (EMET) is slightly too abrupt; PNEUMA is too colloquial.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 48:5 "greatly shaken and afraid" vs. "greatly disturbed and afraid"

- **EMET:** "greatly shaken and afraid"
- **LOGOS:** "greatly disturbed and afraid"
- **PNEUMA:** "deeply shaken and afraid"
- **Greek:** *taraxtheis sphodra kai phoboumenos* — being greatly disturbed/shaken and fearing
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "greatly disturbed and afraid" (LOGOS). *Tarassō* = to disturb, unsettle, throw into confusion; "disturbed" is precise; "shaken" implies more physical movement.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 48:5 "if even this man who keeps the commandments" — framing

- **EMET:** "if even this man who keeps the commandments shall with difficulty be saved"
- **LOGOS:** "if even he who keeps the commandments shall with difficulty be saved"
- **PNEUMA:** "if even the person who keeps these commandments is barely saved"
- **Greek:** *ei ho tēroōn tas entolas molis sōthēsetai* — if the one keeping the commandments is barely saved
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "if even he who keeps the commandments shall with difficulty be saved." EMET and LOGOS agree on "with difficulty"; PNEUMA's "barely" is a legitimate equivalent but loses the emphasis on the struggle.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 48:5 "cares and anxieties" vs. "anxieties and cares"

- **EMET:** "many cares and anxieties came upon me"
- **LOGOS:** "many anxieties and cares came upon me"
- **PNEUMA:** "I was overwhelmed with anxiety and worry"
- **Greek:** *merimēai pollai kai agoōniai* — many worries and agonies/anxieties
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "many anxieties and cares came upon me" (LOGOS). *Agōnia* = anguish/agony/anxiety should come first, as it is the stronger term; EMET reverses the order.

---

## Disagreement 10 — 48:5 "do not worry" vs. "do not be troubled" vs. "don't let those thoughts trouble you"

- **EMET:** "Do not worry about these things"
- **LOGOS:** "Do not be troubled by these things"
- **PNEUMA:** "Don't let those thoughts trouble you"
- **Greek:** *mē tarachthēs dia toutōn* — do not be troubled/disturbed by these things
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "Do not be troubled by these things" (LOGOS). The same verb *tarassō* from 48:5a recurs — the Shepherd directly addresses Hermas's disturbance with "do not be disturbed," a deliberate echo.

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 48.*
